clue.text: Precisely! Second party is entertainment for children

parts.note: an exclamation of agreement, 'just so!', meaning exactly right
the Tories are Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully agrees that a second party will be a fine treat for the youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories are a classic collection of tales for children. TORIES is the everyday name for members of the British Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's book of fanciful animal origin tales was written to be read aloud to young listeners as a bedtime treat.

clue.text: City's verdict that selected Miss World?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a ruling handed down by the French capital
in Greek myth a Trojan prince chose the fairest of three goddesses, jokingly the first beauty contest

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Trojan prince Paris awarded the golden apple to Aphrodite as the most beautiful of three goddesses; the clue pretends Paris is the French city.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical choice of the loveliest goddess is jokingly recast as a beauty pageant ruling made by a capital city.

clue.text: Society has to tolerate a spell of bad language

parts.note: to wear something, as in 'I won't wear it', is to put up with it

explanation.surface: Polite company is obliged to put up with an outburst of cursing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a good curse, an outburst of oaths, is informally called having a swear in Britain.

clue.text: Categories of officers — junior and senior, mostly

parts.note: a sub, short for subaltern, is a junior army officer

indicators.note: mostly says the word for the senior officer loses its final letter

parts.note: a general is a very senior army officer

explanation.surface: A list sorting military officers into ranks from the most junior to the most senior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of officers' tells the solver both junior and senior refer to officers; 'mostly' drops the last letter of GENERAL to leave GENERA.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology the ranks below a genus are its subdivisions, so the word names groupings or classes.

clue.text: Coal kept here in sink?

definitions.meaning: a coal ... is the metal bucket beside a fireplace that holds fuel
to ... a ship is to sink it deliberately by holing it

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the fireside fuel bucket; the other is deliberately holing and sending a vessel down.

clue.text: Symmetry in style of architecture

definitions.meaning: Doric, Ionic and Corinthian are the classical column styles, each called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: A tidy balanced arrangement is called this, and so is each classical column style such as Doric or Ionic.

clue.text: End in tontine, with characters going in some order

indicators.text: with characters going in some order
indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are said to be rearranged into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Instructions about how a tontine, a shared annuity scheme, is wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: A tontine is an investment scheme whose last surviving member takes everything. 'with characters going in some order' rearranges TONTINE into TENTION, placed after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An end can mean an aim or purpose, as in 'to that end', which is a plan or purpose held in mind.

clue.text: Financial regulators operating in accordance with law?

definitions.text: Financial regulators operating in accordance with law?

parts.words: Financial regulators operating in accordance with law?
parts.note: suggests watchdog officials obeying statute, but really means the two economic forces governed by a famous economic law that sets prices

explanation.surface: City watchdogs carrying out their work within the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'law' is the economic law that prices settle where what is offered meets what is wanted, not a statute.
explanation.definitionFit: Availability and buyers' appetite are the forces that set prices in a market, as described by a basic economic law.

clue.text: Border on which people are nervous

definitions.meaning: being 'on' this is to be tense and jumpy

explanation.definitionFit: A rim is a margin or boundary, and someone said to be 'on' it is jittery and anxious.

clue.text: Obliged to jump

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is duty-bound or compelled; the other is to leap forward in a single spring.

clue.text: Drink a lot to overcome record

indicators.note: read as 'come over', so the word for the record is turned around

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker downs pints to get over a setback on their record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome' is read as 'come over', a reversal signal, rather than its usual sense of defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is an old-fashioned verb for drinking alcohol heavily and habitually.

clue.text: Budding medical speciality about to be swallowed up

indicators.note: about says the speciality's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
to merge is to be absorbed into something larger

explanation.surface: A promising young medical specialism is about to be absorbed by a larger one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'nearly' but means 'surrounding', and 'to be swallowed up' is a verb phrase giving a piece, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something budding is just starting to appear or develop, newly coming into being.

clue.text: Chafe end of tender part' of body

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

parts.note: the ankle is the joint between foot and leg

explanation.surface: A sore spot where something rubs at the end of a tender limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To chafe in the figurative sense is to fret or be irritated, which matches feeling lasting resentment.

clue.text: Promise action

definitions.meaning: a pledge or commitment, as in a betrothal or appointment

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a pledge or betrothal; the other is a clash of forces in battle.

clue.text: Epic that a 'translation rendered unemotional

indicators.note: translating a text renders it in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull translation turned a stirring heroic poem into something flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unmoved and indifferent shows no feeling or interest, which is the sense of being listless.

clue.text: Someone weak and pasty?

parts.note: thin means feeble or watery
gummy means sticky like paste

explanation.surface: A description of a person who is feeble and pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' suggests a pale complexion, but here it means sticky like paste.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a placeholder for a person or thing whose name you have forgotten, like 'what's-his-name'.

clue.text: It's necessary to give him a mosque

definitions.text: It's necessary to give him a mosque

indicators.note: necessary to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A community insists that every mosque must have a leader appointed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'It's' cannot stand for a prayer leader; the whole clue is the definition, since such a leader is what a mosque needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The prayer leader of a Muslim congregation is the figure every mosque requires.

clue.text: Island attached to a state

indicators.note: attached to says the island's letters are joined directly onto what follows

parts.note: IOW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast

explanation.surface: An island bolted on to one of the American states.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off southern England, abbreviated IOW.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the fifty constituent units of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: A heartless romance leads to trouble for enthusiastic follower.

indicators.note: heartless says the word for romance loses its central letter

parts.note: a romance is a work of fiction
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A loveless affair brings grief to a devoted fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle T from FICTION, leaving FICION.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee or keen fan of an activity or art is an enthusiastic follower of it.

clue.text: Disinclination to move train that is broken down

indicators.note: a broken-down train is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e., from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A stalled locomotive refuses to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and everyday use it is a body's tendency to stay at rest, a reluctance to start moving.

clue.text: The end of a skier?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a skier is a ball hit high into the air

explanation.definitionFit: The final result is the outcome; read in two parts it is a stroke sent high, a cricket skier.

clue.text: Convert it to the share yielding 10%

indicators.note: to convert something is to change it into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to change an asset into a stake paying ten per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' rearranges IT into TI, which is followed by THE as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditionally a tenth of produce or income was paid to the church as a levy.

clue.text: Monument in terminus made an impression

indicators.note: in says the monument goes inside the word for terminus

parts.note: an end is a terminus or final point
a grave is a burial place marked by a memorial

explanation.surface: A memorial at the end of the line left its mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is to cut a design into a surface, literally making an impression.

clue.text: Nobody was present to make such a plea

definitions.text: Nobody was present to make such a plea

parts.words: Nobody was present to make such a plea
parts.note: reads as an empty courtroom, but means the defence that the accused was somewhere else at the time

explanation.surface: With an empty court, no one could put forward the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that the plea is precisely that the accused was not present at the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the defence that the accused was elsewhere when the offence happened.

clue.text: Tiny stones found in guts

definitions.meaning: small particles of stone or sand

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is small gravel particles; the other is courage and resolve.

clue.text: Art of jazz piano

parts.note: looks like the craft of playing jazz keyboards, but Art is the first name of a famous American jazz pianist

explanation.surface: A treatise on the craft of jazz keyboard playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Art Tatum was a celebrated American jazz pianist; 'Art' is his first name, not skill.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the virtuoso American jazz pianist whose first name was Art.

clue.text: Scotsman is outside right for this country

indicators.note: outside says the Scotsman's letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is out on the right wing for his national side.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a nation in western Asia, formerly Persia.

clue.text: Flier covered tracks about a prison sentence

parts.note: secret means hidden or concealed
RY is the abbreviation for railway
bird is British slang for a jail term, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time

explanation.surface: An escaped convict covered his tracks to avoid going back to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for time in prison. The answer is a long-legged African bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long-legged African raptor, and any bird is something that flies.
